name: ClickClue – Session Replay
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Watch eligible, signed-out visits to understand navigation, clicks and scrolling. Choose ClickClue’s consent banner, a connected existing banner, or recording without asking first. Bookmark recordings and add notes. Recordings stay in WordPress; no external analytics account is required.

Included in Free

  • Session recording and replay with playback controls, click markers and grouped scroll events.
  • Page, device, date, watched and bookmarked filters, plus saved filters.
  • Bookmarks and review notes to keep useful examples together.
  • Three explicit recording modes, visitor opt-out, masking, page exclusions and private-region controls.
  • Configurable sampling, retention and storage budget.

Free has no trial expiry or monthly quota. Your recording mode, visitor privacy choices, sampling, retention, storage and hosting limits apply.

Optional ClickClue Pro add-on

Pro adds grouped clues, heatmaps, structural form insights, journeys, comparisons, optional feedback and team tools. These paid features are separate; Free replay and privacy controls work without Pro. Existing Pro feedback and order-association integrations still require visitor consent; owner-policy recording does not widen those permissions.

Compare Free and Pro.

Privacy

Banner modes require visitor permission. The without-asking mode is an explicit site-owner choice, not evidence that a visitor consented. Existing valid refusals and opt-outs remain respected in every mode. Saved masking choices survive upgrades. Images are excluded by default. SVG, canvas, audio, video, embedded frames, hidden inputs and editable content remain excluded. URL query values and fragments are removed, except a verified public WordPress post or page ID needed to distinguish plain permalinks. Structural classes and IDs can remain for layout; use data-tw-block or exclusion selectors around sensitive attributes.

Free does not intentionally collect raw IP addresses, request bodies, console logs, customer IDs or order IDs. Mask or exclude sensitive details in page text or attributes. A rotating keyed IP hash is kept temporarily for rate limiting. Hosting/server logs are outside the plugin’s control.

The built-in prompt saves site-scoped consent choices for 180 days. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control prevent recording in every mode. Replay privacy remains available when recording without asking first. Stopping or withdrawing stops capture, clears unsent data and requests deletion of the current valid session. Failed deletion remains visibly pending. Older sessions follow retention and administrator deletion. Unfinished requests from older versions can remain unconfirmed with recording off; dismissing that notice does not confirm deletion. Owners should review such requests through their privacy process.

Changing the privacy notice, recording mode or scope invalidates earlier authorisation as applicable. Banner modes can require fresh permission after relevant changes, including image approvals and Pro goals or campaigns. Existing valid refusals remain respected. For an external consent manager, choose Use my existing consent banner and connect window.ClickClue.grantConsent() after replay acceptance and window.ClickClue.withdrawConsent() on refusal or withdrawal. That mode still requires permission; it is separate from Record without asking first. Privacy controls alone do not establish legal compliance for an installation.

Approved public images

Off by default. Administrators can approve public, static WordPress images containing no personal or sensitive content. PHP GD and local uploads are required. Bounded PNG/JPEG copies are prepared locally, without arbitrary visitor-URL fetching or screen capture. Private, masked and excluded regions take priority.

The catalogue allows 256 images and about 46 MiB of data/metadata. Each recording allows 64 used copies and 2 MiB within its budget. Unmatched images stay placeholders. Removing approval removes stored copies, preserving other events; downloaded exports need separate review. Update your notice and test first.

Operation

Uploads use acknowledgements, bounded retries and deduplication. Unsent events stay in memory, up to 2 MiB, and clear on withdrawal. Reconnection can resume capture. Oversized snapshots/backlogs stop capture; browser destruction loses pending data. Replay labels interrupted or unconfirmed delivery.

Cleanup uses hourly WP-Cron and bounded dashboard/session cleanup. Low-traffic sites need a real cron trigger for timely retention. Deactivation keeps data. Delete data when uninstalling controls permanent cleanup.

Local guidance and optional previews

Tutorial progress stays in your browser. The Pro previews switch and dismiss choices stay on-site per administrator, with WordPress privacy export/erasure. Selected previews stay in site/account-scoped browser storage for seven days. Previews send no analytics or email signup.

More Plugins bundles sixteen companion descriptions and logos locally. WooCommerce context and known installed-plugin badges are checked locally. Nothing is installed automatically. Publisher and documentation links open only when selected, without site, user or recording identifiers. Help also includes an offline guide.

After the site’s first counted recording is 30 days old and an administrator reviews ten distinct recordings across five UTC days, an optional review invitation can appear. Counters started in 1.1.5 and survive updates. Choose an honest review, a 30-day reminder or permanent dismissal per administrator. Counts stay local. Help also has a review link.

Translations and development

Translations use clickclue: site language for visitors, user language for the dashboard, English fallback. The languages/ template is not a complete set of human translations. Clear page caches after changing site language.

See BUILD.txt and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt for included source, build and licences. The installed guide is translated; assets/help.html is its English copy.
sections.installation:
1. Activate ClickClue. A new installation opens setup with recording paused and no recording mode preselected.
  2. Choose Ask with ClickClue’s banner, Use my existing consent banner, or Record without asking first. The built-in banner needs a published policy selected in WordPress Settings > Privacy. An existing banner must be connected through the integration APIs in Help; installing it alone is not enough.
  3. Review masking, exclusions, retention and storage. Choose Save & enable recording deliberately. Opening setup or choosing Next does not save or enable recording.
  4. Setup saves 100% sampling for the test. This stays at 100% until you change it in Settings; it is not automatically restored to 10%. Clear page/CDN caches and copy the test link into a signed-out private window.
  5. Follow your chosen mode: allow replay in the built-in banner, grant replay permission through your connected banner, or visit directly in the without-asking mode. Click and scroll, then check for uploaded activity.
  6. Open the replay and check its page, time, masking and actions. Another visitor’s latest recording is not proof of your test. Lower sampling to your intended rate or pause recording when finished.

Before setup, defaults are paused, no mode selected, 10% sampling, seven-day retention and a 250 MiB payload budget. Setup’s explicit final save enables recording at 100% sampling while preserving the reviewed privacy and storage choices. Both editions allow 1–365 days and 1–10,240 MiB. The Size column and replay header show each recording; Total storage covers saved recordings. Your host supplies storage; indexes and backups need extra space.

Network activation is not supported. Activate separately on each WordPress site.

Updating an existing installation

Back up first. Update Free to 1.1.10. This Free-only update does not include a new Pro package; retain your compatible Pro add-on. Existing installations keep their enabled state, sampling, privacy settings, recordings and licence state. The previous built-in-banner setting maps to the banner mode; an installation using external consent keeps that mode. Upgrading never silently selects recording without asking first or forces the first-install wizard. Existing valid refusals remain respected. Clear page/CDN caches and test your saved mode.

Folders are clickclue and clickclue-pro. To migrate from older names, deactivate existing copies, then upload and activate Free followed by Pro. Keep old copies inactive; do not Delete or uninstall them to change folders. Never activate duplicate copies.
sections.faq:
Is Free limited by a monthly recording quota?

No. Your recording mode, privacy choices, sampling, hosting, retention and storage limits apply. Each recording is limited to 30 minutes and 8 MiB. Capture pauses at the storage budget and resumes when space is available.

Where are recordings stored? Do I need a ClickClue account?

Recordings stay in your WordPress database, with WordPress account access. Free sends none to ClickClue or external analytics and needs no external account or licence.

Does recording start immediately after installation?

No. New installations remain paused until you explicitly finish setup. Choose a recording mode, review the settings and select Save & enable recording. Banner modes wait for visitor permission. Record without asking first starts eligible visits under the site owner’s chosen policy; it does not invent a visitor consent decision.

Are signed-in visitors or typed values recorded?

Signed-in visitors and account, login, administration, order-pay and order confirmation pages are excluded. Typed values are masked before upload. Ordinary page text is readable by default; Mask all page text is optional. Explicitly private regions remain protected either way. Review your masking and exclusions before recording real visitors.

Why can a replay look different from my live page?

Replay reconstructs the website; it is not desktop video. Images are excluded by default. Media, fonts, backgrounds or unavailable styles may differ. Test your theme and hosting. Unuploaded interactions cannot be replayed.

Does Pro need activation?

Pro adds the tools listed above and needs matching Free plus a valid first licence activation. Previously activated local tools survive ordinary subscription expiry; updates and support require active entitlement. Explicitly deactivating or forgetting the licence locks Pro without deleting recordings or settings.
sections.changelog:
1.1.10

  • Add a first-install setup wizard with three equal recording choices and no preselected mode. Recording starts only after an explicit save.
  • Keep the same mode selector in Settings; preserve existing banner/external-consent choices and saved settings on upgrade.
  • Support an explicit site-owner policy for recording without asking first while retaining visitor opt-outs, masking, exclusions and server protections. Do not label that policy as visitor consent.
  • Make 100% setup sampling explicit and persistent until changed, and distinguish enabled recording from newly received test activity.
  • Add accessible recording-mode help and actionable privacy-notice checks before built-in-banner setup can finish.

1.1.9

  • Clarify the consent-banner setting and link directly to the installed cookie-banner integration guide. Recording permissions and defaults are unchanged.

1.1.8

  • Make clicks and grouped scroll activity reachable in the replay timeline.
  • Explain upload status and show the last received activity without claiming the entire visit was recorded.
  • Distinguish each recording’s size from total saved storage.
  • Store computed replay layout once and preserve floated product-page columns.
  • Preserve a best-effort interruption notice when recording stops at a size limit or a rejected upload.
  • Schedule periodic recovery snapshots while the visible page is ready, avoiding a large overdue snapshot on the first interaction after a long idle period.

1.1.7

  • Add a saved Pro-preview switch and PRO labels; links wrap on mobile.
  • Add publisher attribution, Help and a local catalogue of sixteen companions.
  • Explain recording blockers on Recordings and link to the relevant controls.
  • Keep Settings focused, with the detailed Free/Pro comparison in Explore Pro.

Earlier release history is included in changelog.txt.
